### Why all 48 are “unchanged”

| Source | What it shows |
|--------|---------------|
| **Scottish Westminster constituencies 2005 – 2024** (Wikipedia) | Lists the 59 constituencies defined by the *Parliamentary Constituencies (Scotland) Order 2005*. The names in the table match the 48 seats above, with no boundary‑changing adjustments recorded until the 2023 boundary review (effective 2024). |
| **2019 United Kingdom general election in Scotland** (Wikipedia) | Under the section “Party – SNP” lists the 48 constituencies that won seats for the SNP in 2019, identical to the names in the 2005 table. |

Because the Fifth Periodic Review (the 2005 Order) remained in force for the 2005, 2010, 2015, 2017 and 2019 general elections, none of the constituencies participating in 2019 had undergone boundary changes between that order and the contest – only the 2023 Parliament Constituency Boundaries Review brought changes for the 2024 election. Therefore every SNP‑held seat (48 of them) was “unchanged” relative to the 2005 order.

## Constituencies and council areas
[edit]
The Fifth Review of the Boundary Commission for Scotland related the boundaries of new constituencies to those of Scottish local government council areas and to local government wards. Apart from a few minor adjustments, the council area boundaries dated from 1996 and the ward boundaries dated from 1999. Some council areas were grouped to form larger areas and, within these larger areas, some constituencies straddle council area boundaries.
The same council area and ward boundaries were in use when the new constituencies were first used in 2005, but ward boundaries have changed since then. New wards were introduced for the 2007 Scottish local government elections.
